title: Tuples and unpacking
short: Fixed little groups: swap, return two values, use as keys.
what: A tuple is a list that cannot change, written with round brackets: (3, 5). Unpacking pulls its items into names in one line. Because it never changes, a tuple can be a dict key or a set item.
analogy: A sealed envelope with a few cards inside. You cannot swap cards once it is sealed, but you can open it and hand each card to a different person.

frames.label: p = (3, 5)
frames.say: p = (3, 5) is a tuple: round brackets, commas between. Read it like a list: p[0] is 3, len(p) is 2.

frames.label: p[0] = 9
frames.say: p[0] = 9 raises TypeError. Contents that never change are the point: safe to share and safe as a key.

frames.label: x, y = p
frames.say: x, y = p unpacks: the first item goes to x, the second to y. The number of names must match.

frames.label: a, b = b, a
frames.say: To swap a and b, write a, b = b, a. The right side is packed into a tuple (5, 3) first.

frames.label: a, b = b, a
frames.say: Then it is unpacked into a and b. No temporary variable needed.

frames.label: nums[0], nums[3] = nums[3], nums[0]
frames.say: The same trick swaps two items of a list: nums[0], nums[3] = nums[3], nums[0].

frames.label: nums[0], nums[3] = nums[3], nums[0]
frames.say: 4 and 2 trade places in one line. Sorting and two-pointer code does this all the time.

frames.label: best = {(0, 1): 4, (2, 2): 9}
frames.say: Tuples can be keys: best[(2, 2)] reads the value stored for grid cell row 2, column 2. A list as a key raises TypeError.

when: Return two things from a function
Use a pair like (row, col) as a key
python:
p = (3, 5)
x, y = p
print(p[0], x, y, len(p))
a, b = 3, 5
a, b = b, a
print(a, b)
nums = [4, 1, 7, 2]
nums[0], nums[3] = nums[3], nums[0]
print(nums)
best = {(0, 1): 4, (2, 2): 9}
print(best[(2, 2)], (1, 1) in best)
try:
    p[0] = 9
except TypeError:
    print("tuples cannot change")
cost: Use a small tuple as a dict key
watch: (5) is the number 5. A one-item tuple needs a comma: (5,).
x, y = [1, 2, 3] raises ValueError: the counts must match.
A tuple that holds a list cannot be a key. Everything inside must be unchangeable too.
